label: Singularities and Intersections
notes: Appendix E spans printed pages 653 through 694 and asks why intersections of distinct J-holomorphic curves in dimension four are isolated and positive. The whole appendix builds local structure theorems near critical points and branch contacts, then converts four-dimensional intersection theory into a controlled algebraic count with signs.

label: The Four-Dimensional Setting
notes: We work in an almost complex four-manifold where curves are real two-dimensional and generically meet in points. The homological intersection number depends only on classes, but the local analytic picture controls how each meeting point contributes. Positivity and adjunction are the two consequences that make this count rigid.

label: Positivity of Intersections
notes: Two distinct closed J-holomorphic curves meet in finitely many isolated points, and every local intersection multiplicity is a strictly positive integer. Summing these local indices recovers the homological number A dot B, so distinct curves can never cancel intersections the way smooth surfaces with opposite signs might.

label: The Local Model
notes: Near a meeting point we model the two branches as graphs over a common coordinate, comparing their leading complex terms. The difference of branches behaves like z to a power m, and the multiplicity equals the order of vanishing of that difference. This local holomorphic picture is the engine behind every positivity statement.

label: Transverse Versus Tangent
notes: A transverse intersection contributes multiplicity exactly one, the minimal positive value. Tangency or higher-order contact raises the multiplicity above one, since the branches agree to higher order before separating. The local index thus measures precisely how strongly the two curves cling together at the shared point.

label: Winding and Contact Order
notes: On a small circle around the meeting point, the difference of the two branches winds positively, and its winding number equals the contact order. This positive winding is the computational face of positivity: the local index can never be negative because a genuine winding count is always nonnegative for distinct branches.

label: Perturbing to Transverse Points
notes: Perturbing the contact equation z to the m minus epsilon splits a single tangential meeting into exactly m simple transverse intersections, each of multiplicity one. This shows the local index m counts hidden transverse crossings, confirming that the contribution is both positive and an honest integer equal to the contact order.

label: The Adjunction Formula
notes: The adjunction formula ties the homological self-intersection A dot A to the genus and the first Chern number through a nonnegative singularity term delta. Delta counts double points and cusps with positive weights, so the formula becomes an exact ledger relating topology, the canonical class, and the curve's local defects.

label: The Adjunction Inequality
notes: Dropping delta yields the adjunction inequality, a bound on the genus in terms of self-intersection and the Chern number. Equality holds exactly when the singularity term vanishes, which happens precisely when the curve is embedded. The inequality is therefore a sharp embeddedness test driven by local positivity.

label: Micallef-White Theorem
notes: The Micallef-White theorem states that a J-holomorphic singularity is, after a homeomorphism of a neighborhood, topologically identical to a holomorphic curve singularity. This transfers the entire classical theory of plane-curve singularities into the almost complex world and justifies treating delta exactly as in algebraic geometry.

label: Proof Architecture
notes: Integrability builds isothermal coordinates, Hartman-Wintner extracts the leading term, local-behavior lemmas normalize one branch, and contact lemmas compare two branches. Micallef-White packages these into a coordinate theorem, from which positivity and adjunction follow as finite local counts rather than fresh analytic arguments.

label: Recap and Outlook
notes: Remember the appendix as a local ledger plus a proof map: every meeting point and singularity contributes a positive integer, embeddedness is equality in adjunction, and the singularity is topologically holomorphic. Later chapters invoke positivity and adjunction freely, trusting this local analysis without redoing it.
